title: The Korean Home Key You Cannot Put on a Keyring

slides.headline: In Korea, your **front-door key** is often a number.
slides.note: Many apartment doors open with a digital lock. You press a code, turn the handle and walk in.

slides.headline: The keyhole is **gone**
slides.body: A black keypad sits where a lock used to be. The door looks ordinary until you reach for it.

slides.headline: You learn a code like a **phone number**
slides.body: It becomes muscle memory: tap the panel, wait for the click, push the door. No metal key to find first.

slides.headline: A visitor gets a **number**, not a spare key
slides.body: Family, friends and house-sitters can enter without collecting a key. The code is the handoff.

slides.headline: keys needed for the **quick trip downstairs**
slides.body: Phone, wallet, nothing — many people step out knowing the door will still open when they come back.

slides.headline: The delivery stays **outside**
slides.body: A parcel can wait at a locked front door. Nobody needs a buzzer, a key exchange or a face-to-face handoff.

slides.headline: Moving day starts with a **new code**
slides.body: The first small job in a new home is not cutting a key. It is choosing the number everyone will remember.

slides.headline: Then the lock tells you: **change the batteries**
slides.body: The trade-off is power. A low-battery warning is a household sound nobody wants to hear at midnight.

slides.headline: Elsewhere, keys prove you **belong**
slides.body: In Korea, remembering four or six digits can do the same job. The proof is in your head, not your pocket.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.

caption:
Korean apartment door locks have quietly changed what a house key looks like. Instead of fishing for metal keys at the door, many people tap a passcode, hear the lock click, and walk in.

That small change affects everything around the door: what you give a guest, how you move in, whether you carry keys for a two-minute errand, and why a low-battery beep can feel like a household emergency.

What does the front-door key look like where you live?
reply:
One detail that did not fit on the cards: many digital locks have an emergency power contact on the outside, so a dead internal battery does not automatically mean sleeping in the hallway. The exact backup method varies by lock.
